notebook.title: A small input controls a larger current
notebook.question: How does raising the input change lamp current when the supply and resistors stay the same?
notebook.prediction: The lamp current will increase because more base current flows.
notebook.explanation: The prediction was supported: lamp current rose from 3 mA to 8 mA. Only input voltage changed; the 5 V supply, 10 kΩ base resistor, and 220 Ω lamp stayed fixed. The supply provides the lamp energy.

observations.note: At 1.0 V, the lamp carries 3 mA. The reversed probes read −0.30 V across the base resistor.
At 1.5 V, the lamp carries 8 mA and VCE drops to 3.24 V.
